date.source: The promotion's own three-part pay-per-view posting, dated 22 January 1999.

appearances.source: the promotion's own 22 January 1999 pay-per-view, as the absent defending champion

matches.note: An open-contract match, two out of three falls. Atlas won the first fall with a top-rope powerbomb; Habeeb the Torturer won the second and, with help from his own stablemates at ringside, the deciding third fall by pinfall.
A submission match. Van Halent won at 12:34 by forcing a submission.

A no-disqualification match billed as making wrestling fans themselves legal weapons. A confused finish saw both a spectator and both assigned referees drawn into the match; the ring announcer declared Flare the winner after a second referee's count, a call the first referee then disputed on air.

A title match whose own stipulation was drawn at random from a fishbowl, landing on a two-part sculpting-and-destruction contest judged on points. Burp the Cuddlesaurus won a close, split decision and the title.
A title match. The champion did not appear; a rival faction's leader sent a stand-in, who was pinned in under a minute.

A tag title match with a 44-minute, 44-second time limit. The challengers won by pinfall in just under ten minutes after one champion's own vintage motor scooter, driven into the ring as a weapon, missed its mark.

The main event, for the promotion's top title, with a 90-minute time limit. The three-time champion's own manager turned on him mid-match, and a short in his opponent's motorized mount sent it crashing down on top of him for the pin at 14:09, crowning a new champion; the manager's heel turn was then revealed as a defection to a rival faction.
